chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and found a 'horn' in her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'This one will not get pregnant. She is returned to her family; if her husband abstains from copulating with her, she is returned to her family.'

I said: 'And if he had consummated the marriage with her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he knew of it before copulating with her, then he copulated with her, he has accepted her. And if he did not know except after copulating with her, then if he wishes afterwards, he keeps her, and if he wishes, he releases her to her family. And for her is what she took from him, by virtue of what she permitted of her private part.'

key_terms.رَضِيَ بِهَا: He accepted her (consented to the condition)

ai.seo_question: What are the marital rights and options if a husband discovers a physical defect in his wife after consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the Shia jurisprudence of *Gharar* (deception/uncertainty) in marriage, specifically addressing the defect of 'Qarn' (often interpreted as uterine horns or a specific anatomical anomaly affecting fertility). It establishes a clear legal distinction based on the husband's prior knowledge: if he knew before consummation, the defect is considered accepted (*Rida*), whereas post-consummation discovery grants him the option to retain or divorce her, with financial compensation (*Mahr*) tied to the validity of the sexual act (*Istihlal*). This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on transparency of physical attributes as a condition for marital validity and the husband's right to rescind the contract if the core purpose of marriage (often procreation) is thwarted by undisclosed defects.
